long_biography.plain_text:
An industrial property needed protection, so Cyril Silberman devised a remote-controlled gate for his fabrication shop. That practical invention became the starting point for Uni-Systems, giving the mechanical engineer a platform for larger moving structures. Military contracts followed, then equipment that helped airlines maintain wide-body aircraft and supported launch facilities at Kennedy Space Center.

Silberman carried the same motion-engineering principles into kinetic architecture. Uni-Systems designed, fabricated and installed machinery for retractable stadium roofs, combining structural movement, controls and continuing maintenance. He later productised that experience in automated canopy systems while continuing to patent mechanisms for aircraft, buildings and other large structures. The pattern across his career is consistent: identify a static infrastructure problem, engineer movement into it and retain responsibility for reliable operation.
